To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method that is suitable for global-scale monitoring of pharmaceuticals in water.
we developed a miniaturised, high-throughput, direct injection HPLC-MS/MS method for 61 APIs and their metabolites for use in global monitoring campaigns of pharmaceutical pollution.

we have developed a novel miniaturised sampling method and high throughput direct-injection HPLC–MS/MS method to enable global monitoring of pharmaceutical pollution in aquatic environments, with the aim of improving the understanding of pharmaceutical pollution on a global scale and reducing the impact of geographic disparities in data availability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method to characterise the occurrence of pharmaceuticals in the aquatic environment.
the development and validation of a high throughput method for the analysis of a wide array of pharmaceuticals in a range of water matrices.

the development of a novel method to enable large-scale monitoring campaigns in the aquatic environment, and the application of this method in the first ever global monitoring campaign of pharmaceutical pollution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this method is suitable for use in large-scale monitoring campaigns to characterise pharmaceutical pollution in aquatic environments globally.

this miniaturised sampling, high throughput and fully automated method is suitable for large-scale aquatic monitoring campaigns of pharmaceutical pollution in different geographical scales and different environmental compartments.

the method is robust and reliable for the quantification and determination of 61 APIs and metabolites in tap water, surface waters and WWTP influent and effluent samples collected globally and that it can be used to generate large-scale monitoring data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a method for the quantitation of pharmaceuticals and metabolites in tap water, surface waters and WWTP influent and effluent samples which can be used globally and has been validated in a variety of different water types.
this novel method is robust and reproducible for the analysis of APIs in tap, surface and WWTP influent and effluent water.
this approach is a cost-effective, rapid and robust method for the quantitation of 61 APIs and their metabolites from water samples in a global monitoring campaign.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a miniaturised sample collection and storage approach can provide a robust, low cost, high throughput, globally accessible and fully validated method for the analysis of 61 APIs in water.
the method is robust, reproducible and can be used for large scale monitoring of pharmaceutical pollution globally.
the proposed method is a robust, low-cost and high-throughput analytical tool that can be used in large-scale monitoring campaigns to characterise levels of pharmaceutical pollution globally.
